claims.text: Formation and crystal-structure selection in noble-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles are governed by the interplay between reduction kinetics and atomic diffusion during growth.
Moderate reduction rates prevent excessive supersaturation and uncontrolled nucleation.
An intermediate thermal dwell permits sufficient atomic diffusion for uniform mixing and formation of a single-phase solid solution.
Deviation from the proposed kinetic pathway causes phase separation, elemental segregation, or morphological irregularities.
The relevant structural mediators are metal-ion reduction timing, nucleation density, and the degree of atomic diffusion during the dwell.
Moderate reduction enables sequential metal-ion reduction and controlled nucleation.
The intermediate dwell provides a window for atomic diffusion and equilibration.
Atomic diffusion and equilibration during the dwell foster a thermodynamically stable, well-ordered, single-phase solid solution.
Excessively rapid reduction produces high nucleation density.
An inadequate dwell restricts atomic mobility and thereby promotes phase separation or segregation.
A moderate ramp rate combined with an effective intermediate dwell will produce nanoparticles with sharp, narrow X-ray diffraction peaks.
A moderate ramp rate combined with an effective intermediate dwell will produce uniform elemental distributions in TEM/EDS measurements.
Sharp, narrow diffraction peaks and uniform elemental maps indicate a single-phase structure.
Ramp rates that are either too rapid or too slow will yield broadened or split diffraction peaks and phase segregation or abnormal morphology.
Current one-step rapid-heating protocols typically produce phase-separated structures, elemental segregation, and uncontrolled particle morphology.
The proposed pathway is applicable specifically to equiatomic noble-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles.
Outside an optimal reduction-kinetics and dwell-time window, kinetic trapping and phase instability are expected.
The optimal ramp rate and dwell duration depend on solvent effects and precursor characteristics.

contradictions.description: The example initial composition contains only five elements at a time (Pt, Pd, Ag, Au, and either Rh or Ir), whereas the requested regime concerns alloys containing more than five elements; the stated boundary does not resolve this scope mismatch.
